answers: News that a shooting left multiple people dead may sound depressingly familiar, but the one outside Baltimore on Thursday is unique in at least one way: The shooter was female. Police say the 26-year-old woman, who has not been identified, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head. Harford County Sheriff Jeff Gahler said she was a temporary employee at the Rite Aid distribution center where the shooting took place, reports the Baltimore Sun. Police say the suspect killed three people, and three others remain hospitalized with wounds not believed to be life threatening. Details and developments: When, where: The Rite Aid distribution center where the shooting took place is at a business complex in Perryman, about 30 miles from Baltimore, reports WBAL. Deputies got there at 9:06am, within 5 minutes of the first call, said the sheriff. He said that deputies fired no shots and that the shooter used a 9mm Glock semiautomatic handgun. Why: Police aren't speculating about a motive. “Normally, she was a nice person, but she came in in a bad mood,” Mike Carre, an employee at a nearby business, tells the Washington Post, recounting what Rite Aid workers told him. "She wanted to pick a fight," he said. "And then she started shooting.” CNN quotes a law enforcement official who describes her as a disgruntled employee; the site says she worked there as a security guard. The woman lived in Baltimore County, and the gun was legally registered to her.

On Thursday, a tragic shooting occurred at a Rite Aid distribution center in Harford County, Maryland, where a 26-year-old woman, identified as Snochia Moseley, fatally shot three co-workers and injured three others before taking her own life. The incident, which took place at the facility near Aberdeen, was one of three workplace shootings in the United States within a 24-hour period, highlighting a disturbing trend of gun violence in the country.

Moseley, a temporary employee with no prior criminal record, was reportedly disgruntled and had a history of unresolved traffic violations and an unpaid tax bill. She used a legally purchased 9 mm Glock handgun, which she brought to the facility with multiple magazines. The shooting began outside the building and moved inside, with police responding within five minutes of receiving the call at approximately 9:06 a.m. No law enforcement officers fired shots during the incident.

The victims included both employees and others, with four taken to Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center, where two were in stable condition and two were seriously injured. One additional victim was in serious condition at Christiana Hospital in Delaware. The shooter died at the hospital from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities have not yet released the names of the victims or the exact motive behind the attack.

The shooting has sparked concern and outrage, with officials and activists emphasizing the need for action against gun violence. Governor Larry Hogan expressed his condolences and support for the affected families and first responders. The incident also drew comparisons to previous shootings in the area, including a 2017 attack at a granite company in Edgewood, Maryland, and a recent shooting at a newsroom in Annapolis.

The Rite Aid facility, which employs around 1,000 people, has been closed for investigation, and grief counselors are being made available to affected employees. Nearby businesses, including Clorox and Zenith Freight Services, also halted operations. A family reunification center was set up for workers and their families, and the area was placed under a temporary lockdown as a precaution.

This tragic event underscores the ongoing issue of gun violence in the United States and has reignited calls for stricter gun control measures and improved workplace safety protocols. As the investigation continues, the community and officials remain focused on supporting the victims and their families while addressing the broader public safety concerns.

Moseley had no prior criminal record, though she had unresolved traffic violations and a civil case related to an unpaid tax bill. Law enforcement did not fire any rounds during the incident.

Rite Aid, the largest tenant in the Enterprise Business Park where the shooting occurred, closed the facility and is assessing when to reopen it. The company has offered grief counseling to affected employees. Other businesses in the area, including Clorox, Zenith Freight Services, and Maines Paper & Food, also halted operations. The facility is shared with several other companies, including a food distributor and a logistics firm.
